Done. Three PNGs are in the working folder at exact sizes: **square.png** 1080×1080, **landscape.png** 1920×1080, **story.png** 1080×1920, all rendered from a single source `card.html`.

**Design**
- `#0F1226` base with two soft violet radial glows and a violet hairline along the top edge.
- Brand lockup: logo mark + divider rule + `FIELDNOTES CONF 2026` in tracked-out bold.
- Portrait cropped to a circle (`object-fit: cover`, face-biased `object-position`) with a violet ring, an outer violet halo and a drop shadow.
- Title set large in Inter Bold with tight tracking; the word "trust" picks up the accent violet.
- Footer sits under a hairline rule: date/venue in muted lavender, violet pill button with a glow.

**Per-size layout** — the three sizes aren't just rescaled; the stage is a CSS grid that re-flows via `grid-template-areas`:
- **Square**: portrait and name/role side by side, title full width beneath, date left / button right.
- **Landscape**: two columns — name, role and title stacked on the left, a 380px portrait spanning both rows and vertically centered on the right. This was the fix for a real defect: in my first pass the portrait sat in a narrow left column and "Maya Okonkwo-Lindqvist" hyphen-broke across two lines.
- **Story**: fully centered column — large 444px portrait, name, role, then the title over four lines, with the date and button stacked at the bottom.

**Verification** — I wrote a throwaway Playwright script that measured every element at each size and asserted: nothing outside the frame, no clipping on elements that actually clip, no pairwise overlap between the brand/portrait/name/title/date/button boxes, the portrait box exactly square, no page scroll, and Inter genuinely loaded (`document.fonts.check` → true, so the text isn't falling back). Its first run was itself buggy — it passed `viewportSize` to `newPage` instead of `viewport`, so all three reported identical 1280×720 boxes and a flood of false failures; after fixing that, all three sizes report clean. I also reviewed every render by eye and bumped the story's portrait and type sizes so the tall canvas didn't feel empty.

Its first run was itself buggy — it passed `viewportSize` to `newPage` instead of `viewport`, so all three reported identical 1280×720 boxes and a flood of false failures; after fixing that, all three sizes report clean. I also reviewed every render by eye and bumped the story's portrait and type sizes so the tall canvas didn't feel empty.
